title: Employment Ontario and cultural tourism grant recommendations
subtitle: Cambridge food bank, Community Safety and Well-Being Plan, Sunnyside Home, youth survey, encampments and homelessness
overview: The Community and Health Services Committee recommended that the Region keep serving as an Employment Ontario provider until at least March 31, 2025. The Region would use that time to assess whether the role remains beneficial and affordable under the new Service System Manager model starting January 1, 2024 {{vote:m3}}. Staff said income and employment security affect health, and that the service supports vulnerable residents.

The committee also recommended guidelines for a one-year Cultural Drivers of Tourism pilot grant program, funded by the Municipal Accommodations Tax {{vote:m2}}. Funding would go to successful applicants on a retroactive basis.

The committee received several reports for information, including the Community Safety and Well-Being Plan's first-year results, the Sunnyside Home Medical Director's report and a youth engagement survey update. After hearing from the Cambridge Food Bank, it directed staff to report on whether the Region could help the food bank's new facility continue and expand its services. Staff will bring an encampments report to the May 24 Council meeting. These recommendations go to Council for a final decision.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended that the Region remain an Employment Ontario provider until at least March 31, 2025 while evaluating whether this stays beneficial and fiscally viable under the new Service System Manager model {{vote:m3}}.

decisions.item: Cultural Drivers of Tourism Pilot Grant Program
decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the pilot program guidelines, with funding from the Municipal Accommodations Tax and evaluation after one year {{vote:m2}}.
